info.name: OAN Registry Dashboards (randomized E2E)
info.description:
End-to-end, randomized tests of the OAN registry dashboards (Farmer, Livestock, Crop Sown) through the public HTTPS gateway `GET {{baseUrl}}/api/charts?charts=<id>,...`.

**Use this collection.** It replaces "Registry Dashboard APIs (Farmer, Crop, Livestock)", which calls the in-cluster `http://<service>.<namespace>` addresses that only resolve inside Kubernetes, and "OAN Dashboards (dev)", which is pinned to one host and one region.

**Environments.** Pick one; nothing else is required:
- *OAN Dashboards - New Dev*: `https://oan-dashboard-development.oanstaging.com`
- *OAN Dashboards - Staging*: `https://oan-dashboard.oanstaging.com`

**What a run does.**
1. *Setup* reads health, config, the filter options and the map units, then fetches every chart unfiltered (the baseline).
2. The baseline picks a random geography: a region, a zone in it, a woreda in that and, when one has data, a kebele. It also picks a farming type and a record state.
3. *Geography scopes* filter every chart to each picked level. *Attribute filters* filter by the picked farming type and record state. *Negative* covers an unknown chart, an unknown region, a hostile filter value and the default chart set.

Run more iterations (`-n 10` in the CLI, or Iterations in the Runner) to cover more units. Each iteration picks again.

**What is asserted.** Expected numbers are never hardcoded; they come from the same run's baseline:
- **Envelope.** Every requested chart succeeds and has the documented fields.
- **Code levels.** Region codes are ET+2 digits, zones +2 more, woredas +2 more.
- **Cross-chart totals.** Within each response, totals agree across charts. For example, `farmerKpis.total_farmers` equals the sum of every farmer breakdown, and `livestockKpis.animals` equals the sum of every livestock breakdown.
- **Scope.** Each scoped KPI equals the baseline row for that unit (0 if the unit has none), and no row falls outside the scope.

**Variables** (environment or `--env-var`). All are optional; leave them empty for random:
- `seed`: replays a run. The seed is printed in the "picked ..." test of every iteration.
- `pick`:
  - `populated`: only units that have data.
  - `all`: any unit on the map.
  - `mixed`: the default.
- `region`, `zone`, `woreda`, `kebele`: pin a level. Levels below a pinned one are still picked at random.
- `farmingType`, `recordState`: pin an attribute filter.
- `charts` (collection variable): narrow the chart list while debugging.

**CLI:** `postman collection run oan-registry-dashboards.postman_collection.json -e new-dev.postman_environment.json -n 10`

The source is `docs/registries/dashboard-postman/` in the Protean workspace repo; rebuild with `build.py`.

item.name: 3 Negative

request.description: A chart no service serves must fail alone, with 'not found'.
A well-formed region with no units must return empty or zero rows, not errors.
A quote-laden filter value must not error or leak rows.
No charts parameter: every chart the gateway serves by default must succeed.

item.description: Contract at the edges: unknown chart, unknown region, hostile filter value, default chart set.

exec: // Send only the filters that resolve to a value: an unset filter must be absent, not "region=".
const kept = pm.request.url.query.filter(p => !p.disabled && pm.variables.replaceIn(String(p.value == null ? '' : p.value)) !== '');
kept.forEach(p => pm.request.url.query.add({ key: p.key, value: p.value }));
// One test script for the whole collection. Each request sets _check (and _level) in its
// pre-request script; this script dispatches on it. Expectations come from the unfiltered
// baseline of the same run, never from hardcoded numbers, so the suite works on any environment.
// The crop geography charts return the AREA under "farmers" and the head count under "farmer_count".
// Per level, the chart of each registry that has one row per unit, and what its row means.
const CODE_RE = { region_code: /^ET\d{2}$/, zone_code: /^ET\d{4}$/, woreda_code: /^ET\d{6}$/, kebele_code: /^ET\d{8}(\d{4})?$/ };
const sum = (rows, f) => rows.reduce((t, r) => t + num(r[f]), 0);
const json = s => { try { return JSON.parse(s); } catch (e) { return null; } };
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { /* asserted below */ }
pm.test('JSON body', () => pm.expect(body !== null && typeof body === 'object', pm.response.text().slice(0, 200)).to.be.true);
const codeKey = row => Object.keys(CODE_RE).find(k => k in row);
pm.test(`no chart failed (${ids.length} requested)`, () => pm.expect(failed, failed.join(' | ')).to.eql([]));
// Special units outside the usual chain are tolerated; a level shift makes most codes odd.
pm.test(`${id}: ${key} at its level`, () => pm.expect(odd.length, `off-level: ${odd.slice(0, 5)}`).to.be.below(Math.max(1, data.length / 2)));
// Totals that must agree inside any single response, filtered or not.
const eq = (name, a, b) => pm.test(`consistent: ${name}`, () => pm.expect(num(a), `${a} vs ${b}`).to.be.closeTo(num(b), 0.01));
const le = (name, a, b) => pm.test(`consistent: ${name}`, () => pm.expect(num(a), `${a} vs ${b}`).to.be.at.most(num(b) + 0.01));
const g = v => sum(rows('farmersByGender').filter(r => String(r.gender).toUpperCase() === v), 'farmers');
// A keeper can hold animals in several units, so per-unit keeper counts may add up to more.
if (ok('livestockBySpecies')) eq('species_tracked = livestockBySpecies rows', l.species_tracked, rows('livestockBySpecies').length);
if (ok('livestockByBreed')) eq('breeds_tracked = livestockByBreed rows', l.breeds_tracked, rows('livestockByBreed').length);
if (!close(byCrop, c.total_area)) console.warn(`cropAreaByCrop covers ${byCrop} of ${c.total_area} ha: plots without a crop are dropped`);
const runSeed = pinnedSeed !== undefined && pinnedSeed !== '' ? Number(pinnedSeed) : (cv.get('_runSeed') ? Number(cv.get('_runSeed')) : Math.floor(Math.random() * 1e9));
const pin = { region: pm.variables.get('region') || '', zone: pm.variables.get('zone') || '', woreda: pm.variables.get('woreda') || '', kebele: pm.variables.get('kebele') || '' };
const codesFrom = (ids, re) => [...new Set(ids.flatMap(id => (baseline[id] || []).map(r => String(r[codeKey(r) || ''] || ''))).filter(c => re.test(c)))];
let pool = mode === 'populated' ? populatedWoredas : units.map(u => u.woreda).filter(w => CODE_RE.woreda_code.test(w));
if (!pool.length && mode === 'populated') { mode = 'all (no populated woreda in the pin)'; pool = units.map(u => u.woreda).filter(w => w.startsWith(pinned)); }
const kebeles = codesFrom(Object.values(GEO.kebele), CODE_RE.kebele_code).filter(k => w && k.startsWith(w));
const pick = { _region: region, _zone: zone, _woreda: w, _kebele: kebele, _farmingType: farmingType, _recordState: recordState };
pm.test(`picked ${label}`, () => pm.expect(region, 'no region could be picked').to.match(CODE_RE.region_code));
pm.test('crop and livestock views on', () => pm.expect(body.registryViews).to.deep.include({ crop: true, livestock: true }));
pm.test('every unit region is a filter option', () => pm.expect(unknown).to.eql([]));
cv.set('_units', JSON.stringify(body.map(u => ({ region: u.region, zone: u.zone, woreda: u.woreda }))));
// Every geography row must lie inside the scope (or be an ancestor of it); Unknown cannot match a filter.
pm.test(`all geography rows inside ${code}`, () => pm.expect(outside, outside.slice(0, 8).join(' ')).to.eql([]));
// Scoped totals equal the baseline row for the unit (0 when the unit has no row).
const expectEq = (label, actual, expected) => pm.test(`${label} = baseline ${code}`, () => {
pm.test(`farmersByType has only ${ft}`, () => pm.expect(rows('farmersByType').map(r => r.farming_type).filter(t => t !== ft)).to.eql([]));
const expected = sum((baseline[id] || []).filter(r => r.record_state === rs), f);
pm.test(`farmers with all filters <= farmers in ${region} (${regionTotal})`, () => {
pm.test('a bad chart id does not fail its neighbours', () => pm.expect(ok('farmerKpis'), chart('farmerKpis') && chart('farmerKpis').error).to.be.true);
const leaked = ids.filter(id => (chart(id) && chart(id).data || []).some(r => Object.values(r).some(v => typeof v === 'number' && v > 0)));
pm.test('no chart returns data outside any unit', () => pm.expect(leaked).to.eql([]));
else pm.test(`known check "${CHECK}"`, () => pm.expect.fail(`no check named "${CHECK}"`));

variable.description: Integer. Empty = new random seed per run; set it to replay a run (the seed is printed in the Pick test).
populated = only units with registry data, all = any unit of the map, mixed = 50/50 per iteration.
Pin a region P-code (ET04). Lower levels are still picked inside it.
Pin a farming type (MIXED); empty = random from farmersByType.
Pin a record state (ACTIVE); empty = random from the baseline.
Charts requested by every chart call; narrow it to debug one chart.
